scope: Additional source-based dates before author-lifespan fallback; no corpus modifications.

matchingRules.priority: Validated quoteIds + authorPattern + textPattern guards first, then author/work context rules, then conservative source extraction, finally lifespan estimate.
matchingRules.dateMeaning: Attested source/work date, not a claim of first-ever utterance or first publication of modern paraphrase.

extractionGuards.recommendation: Inspect source, descriptions and citations. Existing classify() ignores citations entirely.
Strip trailing punctuation-only wrappers such as (;), but do not remove substantive parentheses containing edition or competing dates.
Prefer a clearly attached letter/speech/interview date over its later reprint; retain both typed dates. Do not take the minimum or maximum arbitrary year.
extractionGuards.testInput: Letter to Pamela Clemens Moffet, 9 November 1869, in Mark Twain’s Letters (1917)

extractionGuards.recommendation: Years describing a book’s historical subject are not its publication. Parse a publication-tail year only when unambiguous.
extractionGuards.testInput: How Science Was Born in 300 BC ... (2004)

extractionGuards.recommendation: Lifetime, posthumous anthology, ebook update and narrated event dates remain separate. Prior reviewed ancient rules must win over modern carriers.
Reject page/section/Bekker and bibliographic volume numbers; require digit boundaries.
If multiple equally plausible dates survive, estimate after source checks rather than manufacture an exact date. Do not resolve conflict by smallest year.

Retain source-based versus author-lifespan-estimated metadata. Verify author identity/type, normalize punctuation aliases, and never treat a quotation date as verified merely because a birth/death estimate is numerically plausible.

authorEstimates.basis: Author-era ESTIMATE, not a verified quotation date. Encyclopaedia Iranica reports that many scholars favor around 1000 BCE, while plausible competing chronologies span the thirteenth to sixth centuries BCE. Use -1000 only as a representative sorting year for the attributed author, not a birth year or exact Gathas composition date.
authorEstimates.note: All 10 corpus records cite The Gathas/Yasna. Historical chronology is disputed, and the English translations are much later; neither translation date nor a precise ancient quotation date is established.

authorEstimates.basis: Author-era ESTIMATE, not a verified quotation date. The American Bible Society places the book approximately 470–440 BCE; USCCB describes a possible date before, during, or after Nehemiah's first return in 445 BCE and warns that Malachi may be a pseudonym. -450 is a representative fifth-century BCE activity/context year, not a known birth or utterance date.
authorEstimates.note: All 10 corpus records explicitly cite Book of Malachi with chapter/verse. The original author may be anonymous. These are English NKJV renderings, not evidence that the English wording existed in antiquity.

authorEstimates.basis: Author-era ESTIMATE, not a verified quotation date. The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts cultural-history lecture identifies Sarvajna as a sixteenth-century Kannada poet. 1550 is the representative midpoint of that broad century; no birth/death dates are inferred.
authorEstimates.note: All 10 corpus records cite Tripadis (6) or Flowers of Wisdom (4). The older Kannada-literature study on a government academy library site explicitly discusses disputed chronology, manuscript compilation and inauthentic later verses. The estimate does not date individual verses or English translations.

authorEstimates.basis: Author-era ESTIMATE, not a verified quotation date. The corpus-linked Wikiquote page explicitly identifies William Adams as the Pembroke College master. Pembroke's own history gives birth 17 August 1706 and death 13 January 1789. Applying the requested lifespan heuristic gives round(1706 + .75*(1789-1706)) = 1768.
authorEstimates.note: Identity remains attribution-dependent: all 10 corpus passages come from the 1895 Dictionary of Burning Words, which does not identify an original work in these records. Do not silently switch to the American minister William Adams (1807–1880), sailor, or other namesake. The 1895 anthology is not an original quotation date.

authorEstimates.basis: Author-activity ESTIMATE, not a verified quotation date or lifespan estimate. Google Books and WorldCat identify Roy T. Bennett as author/self-publisher of The Light in the Heart, paperback ISBN 9780987917768, published 2 February 2020. Use 2020 only as an attested modern author-activity anchor when a numerical fallback is mandatory; no birth/death facts are asserted.
authorEstimates.note: All 49 corpus records have only Goodreads community attribution. Goodreads lists a 2016 digital edition, so 2020 is explicitly a later verified catalog activity anchor, not first publication. No checked primary book text matched these 49 records; therefore no verified quoteMappings were added for Roy. Retain estimate labeling on every affected card.
